finalists.label: Myopericarditis
finalists.why: It has the most specific for evidence, including new pericardial friction rub, Initial troponin levels, and diffuse ST-segment elevation.

finalists.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
finalists.why: It has strong for evidence, including sudden chest pain, Initial troponin levels, and acute thrombotic total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery.

frontier_selector.why: Myopericarditis is chosen because it accounts for both myocardial and pericardial findings, such as new pericardial friction rub and diffuse ST-segment elevation, which are not fully explained by Acute Coronary Syndrome.
